# The auto-generated catalog TOCs (concepts.md / stories.md / decisions.md)

## Description

Beside each durable catalog directory sits a generated one-file table of contents: `.ok-planner/design/concepts.md`, `stories.md`, `decisions.md`. Purpose: "the one-shot-readable catalogs consulted by skills that read the design docs (sprint, audit, prove); they let agents know what artifacts exist without reading every full file." Format is fixed: a header declaring generation ("Generated by `discover-design` and refreshed whenever a sprint's deltas touch the catalog. Do not edit by hand — changes will be overwritten"), a usage instruction ("Read first. Then either grep for the matching annotation ... or read `<dir>/<slug>.md` for the full body"), then alphabetical bullets `- <slug> — <one-sentence summary, ≤120 chars>` with optional `(aliases: ...)` parentheticals (aliases mainly for concepts). Summaries are drawn from each artifact's leading line (concept "What it is" first sentence; story "As ... I want ..." line; decision Choice line).

Together with in-source annotations, the TOCs "replace the need for an external index": the TOC answers "what exists," the annotation grep answers "where is it load-bearing." `concepts.md` has extra standing: the materialized session-start hook injects it into every session with the framing "Before defining or invoking any term that appears here, open `.ok-planner/design/concepts/<slug>.md` and read it; do not paraphrase from prior context."

The TOCs are audited: the shared compliance reviewer checks (for catalogs with in-scope files) that every bullet's slug matches a live artifact, every live artifact has a bullet, retired-only entries sit in a "Retired" section rather than the live list, and the one-line definitions obey self-containment ("no paths, no external-doc refs").

## Code surface

- `plugins/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md` step 7 (generation) and the annotation-convention section (index-replacement rationale).
- `plugins/ok-planner/scripts/hooks/session-start` (concepts.md injection).
- `skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md` "TOC consistency" checks.

## Prose surface

- The generated files' own headers (per the step-7 template).

## Adjacent topics

- `design-corpus`, `discover-design` (the generator), `session-context-injection`, `self-containment-rule`, `concept-artifact`.

## Observations

- Refresh responsibility is split in prose: discover-design generates; the header claims sprints refresh "whenever a sprint's deltas touch the catalog," but no sprint boilerplate, certify step, or plan-sprint step names TOC regeneration — the compliance reviewer's consistency check is the only mechanism that would notice a stale TOC after a sprint.
- The reviewer's "Retired" section convention (retired-only entries listed under a Retired heading) appears only in the reviewer prompt; the step-7 generation template has no Retired section — the two shapes of the same file disagree at the edges.
